items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: I was influenced by Philip Gordon who was a concert pianist.

ctx.x: All right. What do you consider your more important influences in music, Godfrey?

That's hard to answer. I was influenced by Philip Gordon who was a concert pianist. But I mean, during my early days, I mean, I couldn't, I didn't get, I really didn't get around like a lot of these guys did. I was, I was always an uptown boy. I never was downtown. Those that lived like back of town and things in it, they were in a different environment than we were up in the university section. I mean, we didn't, we didn't really go for that particular environment. And you didn't get the chance. I mean, like…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: I played before Philip Gordon... In fact, he gave a concert and I was at the concert... after the concert, we were talking and talking

ctx.x: It's getting worse today. That's right. It's getting worse today. You'll see Ray Franson go on a job. I used to tell Ray, all I need is a bass drum and a snare drum. Oh, I have to bring the other equipment with me. And he sets up like this. So I have a snare drum bought from Grunewalds, Mr. Eckert. Old man Eckert. I think he sold every musician in town his first instrument. And my daddy bought me a snare drum. And he wouldn't buy me a set of drums. So my sister was studying piano. And I started looking at her…
Did he play trumpet, Vic, the young one?
